_versions: `version` is what Thunderstore calls the release and is what the modpack pins. `plugin_name` and `plugin_version` are what BepInEx prints in LogOutput.log, which is what scripts/mods-verify.mts compares against. They differ: the loader is packaged as 5.4.2350 and logs 5.4.23.5. A null plugin_name means the entry cannot be verified from the log, and the verifier reports that rather than passing it.

mods.why: The BepInEx loader itself. Everything below is inert without it.
mods.upgrade_5_4_2351: Only three files differ from 5.4.2350: the two core DLLs above and the Linux doorstop library, which is now stock UnityDoorstop 4.5.0 rather than the pack's own build. The Windows winhttp.dll, doorstop_config.ini and both start scripts are byte-identical. The server preloads the doorstop library from valheim.service, so it is the file that decides whether BepInEx starts at all; the old and new builds read the same 17 DOORSTOP_* environment variables (read with strings), so the unit's existing ExecStart drives the new one unchanged. Both core DLLs still report 5.4.23.5, so the banner, and therefore plugin_version and the verifier, cannot tell 5.4.2350 from 5.4.2351. Prove the new loader by these hashes on the box and by the lines only 5.4.2351 prints: the plugin GUID after each 'Loading [...]', and the '(N loaded, N skipped, N failed)' counts on 'Chainloader startup complete'. mods-verify.test.mts pins the GUID-suffixed load line.

Two behaviour changes ship with it and NEITHER bites this box, both read off the regenerated config on 2026-09-22. difficultyScaleRange defaulted to 2 metres whenever the Game section was enabled, which was a bug, and now defaults to 100; here [Game] carries enabled = false, so the 200 set in that section is inert and always was. Oven settings now affect only the oven rather than every fuel-burning cooking station. The new [FrigidKiln] and [FrostFoundry] sections for the 1.0.15 Deep North stations were written into the config at lines 912 and 957, which is independent evidence the new DLL generated it rather than inheriting the old one. enforceMod = true at line 2041, so the client pack has to match this pin exactly.

The 8-minute base does not scale, so a low-comfort campfire gains little. The operator chose 120 over 150 (50 minutes at comfort 18) to keep it a little lower.

Every version on Thunderstore is dated 2026-09-16 to 2026-09-21, and recent changelog entries fix "disappearing structures" and "duplicate portals on ships", so the mod is young and still settling. mods.conflict: ValheimPlus free placement rotation is lost while this mod is installed, which is why the why above warns players. The pinned DLL patches Player.UpdatePlacementGhost, including a transpiler (ShipBuildingMod.Player_Patches.UpdatePlacementGhost_Transpiler), and that is the method ValheimPlus's Player_UpdatePlacementGhost_Transpile rewrites. BepInEx breaks load-order ties by GUID, so ShipBuildMod (com.custom.shipbuildmod) loads ahead of ValheimPlus (org.bepinex.plugins.valheim_plus), at server log lines 23 and 48, and ValheimPlus then fails to find the code it expects. Proven on the server by a before and after: the first boot with Build On Ship, 2026-09-25 05:37Z, logged 'Failed to apply `Player_UpdatePlacementGhost_Transpile`. Free placement rotation will not work.' twice, while the journal shows that line on no earlier boot back to 2026-09-10. That includes all 71 boots since a config snapshot first shows [FreePlacementRotation] enabled (2026-09-12 01:58Z), the last of them at 00:03Z the same day with every mod but this one. The loss is real, not cosmetic: enabled = true in the server's ValheimPlus config (read 2026-09-25), and serverSyncsConfig pushes it to clients. A client logging the same line is expected, because the pack loads the same two mods in the same GUID order, but it is UNVERIFIED; the first player to press LeftAlt while placing a piece settles it. Shipped anyway on the operator's call, 2026-09-25: 'Ship both anyway', then 'if it breaks we can always remove it'. Removing this mod restores rotation but may strand pieces built on ships (see note), so take a world backup first.
mods.note: The DLL's BepInPlugin attribute is com.custom.shipbuildmod, ShipBuildMod, 4.0.0, so the log shows 4.0.0 against Thunderstore's 3.4.3. Read off the DLL, then confirmed on the first server boot with it (2026-09-25 05:37Z), which logged 'Loading [ShipBuildMod 4.0.0]' and the mod's own 'ShipBuildMod v4.0.0 loaded successfully.' It declares no BepInProcess restriction, so it loads under the dedicated server. It carries no ServerSync and no Jotunn NetworkCompatibility, so nothing refuses a client that lacks it; what such a client sees on a built-on ship is UNVERIFIED. The ship link is stored in ZDO fields (ShipBuild_ParentUUID, ShipBuild_ShipUUID, ShipBuild_LocalPos, ShipBuild_LocalRot), so assume removing the mod strands built pieces and take a world backup before uninstalling. Ship portals are ordinary portal pieces, so PortalProgression's ore gate should apply to them unchanged; UNVERIFIED.

mods.why_this_fork: Searica-AdvancedTerrainModifiers was pulled on 2026-10-07 (see removed_mods) after two players saw different heights in one place. Read from the DLLs with Mono.Cecil on 2026-10-15: Searica 1.5.6 still claims zone ownership in a TerrainComp.ApplyOperation prefix on every terrain edit, vanilla ones included, and still applies the brush radius from the executing machine's scroll state. This fork claims ownership only for operations that carry its own settings (its tools, or a resized brush), serialises the radius, power and delta into the operation so the zone owner applies the editor's brush, rejects malformed values, and checks wards against the whole brush. It still claims ownership for its own edits, so two players terraforming the same zone at once remain untested.

mods.why_server_side: Client-only was tried first, on the reasoning that the season derives from world age so clients would agree without server sync. Measured 2026-09-18: seasons never advanced, sitting on the configured Summer for days while the client logged a healthy load. Installed server-side the same night, after which the server logs 'Seasonal Timer Awake'. The mod's README lists season_winter and siblings as GLOBAL KEYS, which only a server writes, and every config entry is marked [Synced with Server] with the in-game set command admin-only. Those point the same way but do not by themselves prove the old reasoning wrong; the proof is a season actually flipping, which had not yet happened when this was written.
mods.note: Ships a config/Seasonality texture tree alongside the DLL; a mod manager places it, a hand install must copy it into BepInEx/config. Season lengths live in the server's copy of the config as a Vector3 of days, hours, minutes, with 30 real minutes to the in-game day. All four are set to two days, against a stock default of five in-game hours that cycles a whole year every 25 real minutes. 3.8.3 adds a Warm_Twilight_SnowStorm environment because vanilla's Twilight_SnowStorm became freezing in Valheim 1.0, and instructs you to reset configs or change winter weather by hand. Checked against this estate's config on 2026-09-18 and it does NOT apply: Twilight_SnowStorm appears nowhere here, every [Winter] weather list already reads WarmSnow:1,Twilight_Snow:0.5,WarmSnowStorm:0.1, and Always Cold and Wet Freezes are both Off. Re-check that grep rather than the changelog if the warning resurfaces.

mods.note: Requires Direct3D 11; its readme states Vulkan is not currently validated, so a client launching with -force-vulkan may misbehave. Windows only. Declares no Jotunn dependency and no network sync. More usefully than that reasoning, it was OBSERVED on 2026-09-19 that a client lacking this batch's mods connected and spawned normally (05:40:44Z), and neither new server-side DLL carries a Jotunn NetworkCompatibility string, so nothing here enforces a version match. Its own readme says do NOT install it on a dedicated server; it has no server-side behaviour. The Enhanced Environment colour-grading feature ships Enabled = false and was deliberately left off: it is the one opinionated feature and visibly recolours the game. 0.5.15 through 0.5.17 tune the three features that ship on by default: cloud shadows now form in broad bands rather than one uniform dapple size, the finest shadow octave is dropped when the mask cannot resolve it, which removes shimmer at high ShadowDrawDistance, and underwater caustics now fall off on vertical faces instead of lighting walls like floors. Its zip uses Windows path separators, the same trap as Jotunn's. 0.5.18 only raises the default Water Caustic Lighting intensity to 1.8; a client with an existing config keeps its saved value, so for current players it changes nothing.

mods.why: Grass density and draw distance, so clutter stops popping in a few metres ahead of the player. mods.note: UNINSTALLING THIS SERVER-SIDE PERMANENTLY DESTROYS EVERY SHRINE PLAYERS HAVE BUILT. The shrines are new prefabs, and Valheim deletes ZDOs it cannot instantiate, silently and with no recovery. That is not a hypothetical: the mod's own 0.8.3 changelog is describing what already happened to its users, because 0.8.2 and earlier carried [BepInProcess("valheim.exe")], which makes BepInEx skip the plugin entirely under valheim_server.exe, so it could not load on a dedicated server at all. Treat removal as a destructive operation needing a world backup, never as a rollback. The same reasoning is why it is side 'both' rather than client-only. Version enforcement is ServerSync's, not Jotunn's ModCompatibility: the DLL declares no NetworkCompatibility attribute, and the disconnect path it does carry refuses a client whose ForsakenShrines version differs from the server's, while a client with the mod absent entirely can still connect. So the pack and the box must move together, but a player who never installs it is not locked out. Placement is constrained: natural terrain only, open sky above, and a Stonecutter in range; shrines sit in the vanilla stone hammer tab because Valheim 1.0 hard-limits build categories. Every setting except 'Mod Enabled' is server-synced; that one is client-local and needs a relaunch. 0.8.5 fixes one arm of that destruction: setting 'Mod Enabled = false' on a dedicated server used to skip prefab registration, so the server deleted every shrine ZDO it could not resolve. A dedicated server now ignores that setting, loads anyway, and logs why. The guidance above is unchanged and is now what upstream says too: take the mod off a server by removing the DLL, never by flipping the setting. 0.8.4 added a 'Lock Configuration' setting under General, on by default and held by the server.
mods.symptom_to_remember: Spinning camera plus a character frozen in the wake-up pose on login, on Valheim 1.0, means SOME installed mod is registering build pieces through Jotunn's PieceManager, whose patch targets a field Valheim 1.0 removed; it throws every physics tick and aborts player spawning whenever a Hammer is equipped. It is not specific to this mod. ForsakenShrines 0.8.1 did it, 0.8.2 stopped using PieceManager, and Jotunn 2.30.0 fixes it for mods that still do. Worth knowing before that symptom gets chased as a graphics or client problem.

mods.why_linux_is_fine: The package is 24.8 MB and most of it is a win-x64 LibVLC runtime, which cannot execute on this Linux box. It still loads, for reasons that were CHECKED rather than assumed. The assembly carries no BepInProcess attribute and names neither valheim.exe nor valheim_server.exe, so BepInEx does not skip it under valheim_server.exe; that is the exact way ForsakenShrines 0.8.2 failed here, so it was the first thing looked for. It does carry IsDedicated, IsServer and ZNet, so a server branch exists in the code. The readme scopes the VLC runtime to 'every client' and describes the server's job as simulating station playback position and sending it to players, which is bookkeeping rather than decoding. The libvlc tree is installed on the server anyway, inert, because the readme also says clients and servers must have identical files and 40 MB of dormant Windows DLLs is the cheaper risk.
mods.linux_boot_evidence: First server boot with it, 2026-09-22 05:55Z. The win-x64 LibVLC runtime was the open question and it is answered: 48 files and 31 MB of Windows natives sit in plugins/libvlc on a Linux box and nothing tried to touch them. A whole-word grep for vlc, libvlc and LibVLCSharp across the boot returns NOTHING, so no VLC initialisation was attempted and none failed. OdinOnDemand's own logger printed one line, its load line, which on its own would be weak evidence. The stronger evidence is that it created BepInEx/config/OdinOnDemand/ at 05:55 holding four files, including recipes.json and recipes_item.json: a mod that has written out the recipes for its own buildable pieces has run well past construction. Contrast ForsakenShrines in the same boot, which narrates every prefab it clones; OdinOnDemand is simply a quiet mod.

Our own package: source in the local directory ~/Developer/.orchestration/cultivated-ground-fix, published under the estate's Thunderstore team.

mods.note: Cause, from a probe plugin run on the operator's client on 2026-10-16: Tunnelheim's Postfix on Heightmap.IsCultivated discards the game's answer inside its 16 m voxel columns and returns whether the FIRST non-zero paint mark scanning down a 3 m column (0.5 m cells, 7 cells) is code 2. After digging and flattening with the pickaxe, 564 of 600 logged cells held a stale dirt mark (code 1) at the top of the window above six cultivated marks (window [1,2,2,2,2,2,2]) while the game's own answer was true, so cultivated ground read as dirt. This mod runs after Tunnelheim and returns true when a cultivated mark sits within 1.5 m above or below the queried point. A 0.5 m window was tried first and failed for the PlantEasily grid (F9), which probes at other heights; the 1.5 m window turned its red cells white. Confirmed by the operator in game: single planting and the PlantEasily grid both work. It reads Tunnelheim's internals (VoxelWorld.IsVoxelColumnAt, ChunkOf, s_chunks, chunk Paint) by reflection and disables itself with a logged error if they change. The server is not touched: plants are checked on clients, but that is unverified, so a client without the mod could still see a plant it owns as unhealthy. It does not remove the stale marks, so a Tunnelheim fix upstream would make it redundant. Not reported upstream yet.
mods.upgrade_1_1_0: Published 2026-10-18. Adds a second fix: PlantEasily refused bushes, fiddlehead and other pickables with 'needs more room to grow' on ground dug with Tunnelheim. PlantEasily's ModUtils.PositionHasCollisions checks a tiny capsule at the planting point against layers that include static_solid, and Tunnelheim's dug ground is a VoxelChunk collider on static_solid. Tunnelheim's own PlantEasily compatibility only covers the Plant path (ModUtils.HasGrowSpace), not pickables. 1.1.0 postfixes PositionHasCollisions and clears the refusal only when every hit is a VoxelChunk, so a real obstacle still blocks. Config General/PickablesOnDugGround, default true. Confirmed in game by the operator on jetragon. An unpublished draft that overrode Plant.HaveGrowSpace was dropped: that check never refused anything, about 1.25 million calls with 0 overrides.

mods.why: Trains: stone track laid with the hammer, named stations, a coal locomotive, storage, restaurant, portal and flatbed wagons. Added 2026-10-19 at the operator's request. It answers the same overland-travel complaint as OdinHorse, at a larger scale, for routes the group builds once and rides repeatedly.
mods.risk: REMOVAL DESTROYS BUILDS, and the package is very young. Track, stations, locomotives and wagons are new prefabs, so taking the mod off the server deletes every one of them and whatever sits in the 18-slot wagons, the same failure Forsaken Shrines warns about; removal is a backup-first operation, never a rollback. First published 2026-10-09; 0.2.2 is from 2026-10-19 and the fifteenth release in ten days (0.1.0 to 0.2.2), with 164 downloads at install. The GitHub repo (VladasZ/railroads) holds only a README and images and has no license, so behaviour can be read only from the DLL. Trains keep running and the server plans routes with nobody near, so server CPU and memory with a running train are untested.
mods.conflict: None observed yet; the overlap is in Harmony patches, which chain. Its 75 patch targets include Player.HaveRequirements, Player.TryPlacePiece, Player.PlacePiece, Inventory.MoveItemToThis and Container.Interact, all of which Runic Storage Network also patches for network building, and Player.PieceRayTest, Player.UpdatePlacementGhost, Player.FindClosestSnapPoints and WearNTear.UpdateSupport, which BuildOnShip patches. The flatbed wagon is a moving build deck like BuildOnShip's ship decks, and the portal wagon patches ZDOMan.AddIfPortal and ZDOMan.GetPortals. Building near or on a train, and RSN building beside track, are the cases to watch in game.

mods.risk: REMOVAL DELETES ITEMS: the seven gliders are new item prefabs, so removing the mod deletes any glider a player holds. Since 1.0.6 every glider equips in the cape (shoulder) slot, which the AdventureBackpacks and Utgarde backpacks also use, so a player likely wears either a backpack or a glider, not both (unverified in game). The package is young: 1.0.0 was published 2026-08-19, 1.0.6 on 2026-10-16, and four of the seven changelog entries (1.0.1 to 1.0.4) are blank; 1.0.2 was never published. Gliding drains stamina (3 per second) by default; the config can disable that. It prefixes ZNetScene.RemoveObjects, which runs every frame on the server, to prune null instances before vanilla runs; a fault there is the first suspect for a server stall or a loading-screen hang after install.

Two players with 1.5.5 saw different terrain heights in the same place. Read from the decompiled DLL, not reproduced: its prefix on TerrainComp.ApplyOperation calls ClaimOwnership() before every edit, so the editing client applies the change locally instead of routing it to the zone's owner the way vanilla does (RPC_ApplyOperation runs only on the owner). Two players terraforming near each other can both believe they own the zone, keep their own heights and ignore each other's updates. Its radius and sharpness are also applied from the executing client's local scroll state (InternalDoOperation prefixes). Do not reinstall it for a multiplayer world without testing two players editing the same zone.

removed_mods.why: It takes chests. Whenever a signed chest's contents change, it rebuilds the content list and, if the text stored on the chest differs, calls ContainerRegistryProcessor.RequestOwnership(chest), which asks the current owner to release the chest so the server can write the new text (end of Process in ServersideQoL.ContainerSigns/ContainerAndSignProcessor.cs upstream, read 2026-10-09). An RSN pull or villager deposit into a signed chest can therefore trigger a takeover when it changes the displayed text, the same family as AutoSort. The rate was not measured here: the restart overwrote the pre-removal log. Reinstall only with RSN and ValheimVillages gone. The signs it had placed are ordinary sign pieces and stay in the world with their last text; not checked in game.

removed_mods.why: The operator asked for it to be turned off. Read from the decompiled DLL: the replant patch on Destructible.Destroy returns early unless Player.m_localPlayer exists, so a dedicated server never replants and the mod only acts on each player's own client. Its config entries are bound directly, not through ServerSync's AddConfigEntry, so the server could not switch it off for players either. Dropping it from the pack is what stops replanting; a client still on an older pack keeps replanting until it removes the mod or sets General/Enabled = false. Removing a world-object mod can delete placed objects, but this one only spawns vanilla saplings, so the world needs no restore.
